# Catalogue

Every drawing in the Plotter catalogue, exported as a resolved static SVG at its native 560 × 440. Codes match the website. When a brief names a code (“like TIM-06”), open that file and borrow its construction relationship, not its subject.

Codes are a three-letter family prefix and a number, without gaps within a family. Drawings retired as near-duplicates keep their former codes in the [code map](../history/code-map.md) and are not exported here. The [approved references](../approved-references.md) remain the style anchors; a catalogue drawing is an example, not a new reference selection.

## Geometry (GEO)

| Code | Drawing | What it explains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [GEO-01](GEO-01.svg) | Circle, square, line | Fundamental geometry, connected by radius, tangency, and a shared construction grid. |
| [GEO-02](GEO-02.svg) | Tangency | Two radii share a baseline and an inclined tangent. The contact geometry connects unequal circles through one construction rule. |
| [GEO-03](GEO-03.svg) | The corner rule | One enlarged corner reveals the radius, offset, and tangent points behind a familiar interface shape. |
| [GEO-04](GEO-04.svg) | A system of proportions | Four squares grow from one shared unit. A single diagonal connects the scale into a structural rhythm. |
| [GEO-05](GEO-05.svg) | A circle, extended | A circle and its wider rounded-rectangle state share one height while their corner radii change. |
| [GEO-06](GEO-06.svg) | A curve from three radii | Three circular arcs share tangent directions at their joins, producing one uninterrupted curve. |
| [GEO-07](GEO-07.svg) | The shape between circles | Two equal circular regions reveal an unhatched lens where their boundaries overlap. |
| [GEO-08](GEO-08.svg) | One interval left open | A field of tangent circles keeps its repeated pitch while one missing member interrupts the lower row. |
| [GEO-09](GEO-09.svg) | One rise, one run | Six equal rise-and-run pairs construct a staircase along one repeated slope. |
| [GEO-10](GEO-10.svg) | One piece short | The pip sequence continues across one absent domino, leaving its position unmistakable. |

## Typography (TYP)

| Code | Drawing | What it explains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [TYP-01](TYP-01.svg) | Anatomy of a letter | A custom lowercase a exposes its circular bowl, counter, stem, and optical overshoot. |
| [TYP-02](TYP-02.svg) | A mark in the making | Two concentric arcs and a deliberate opening establish the logic of a simple geometric C. |
| [TYP-03](TYP-03.svg) | A from three strokes | Two parallel-sided diagonal strokes and one horizontal stroke make an outlined capital A; the crossbar is identified by hatching. |
| [TYP-04](TYP-04.svg) | One arch, three glyphs | A shared circular shoulder and a constant stem width generate n, h and m, with the h selected to show the construction. |
| [TYP-05](TYP-05.svg) | The joining stroke | The f and i share one continuous crossbar, joining the two glyphs into a single constructed ligature. |
| [TYP-06](TYP-06.svg) | A monogram in the void | An M is defined by the transparent space within a hatched field; its straight stems and surrounding margin follow the same unit. |
| [TYP-07](TYP-07.svg) | The center you see | A rightward shift brings a triangle’s area centroid to the center of its frame, providing a geometric starting point for optical alignment. |

## Interfaces (INT)

| Code | Drawing | What it explains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [INT-04](INT-04.svg) | Recombination | Identity, visibility, and action combine into one compact panel. Each of the three fragments keeps its role in the assembled result. |
| [INT-09](INT-09.svg) | A conversation, constructed | Two rounded message blocks pair with circular avatars. Shared radius, text inset, and avatar spacing construct the conversation without pointed tails. |
| [INT-01](INT-01.svg) | The exploded interface | A pill, row, and toggle projected onto a shared frame. Separate elements follow a common set of rules. |
| [INT-02](INT-02.svg) | An assembly of parts | An icon, a label, and a status pill align into one row, shown as an exploded technical drawing. |
| [INT-03](INT-03.svg) | A modular tray | Different interface fragments occupy a shared grid, like precisely fitted pieces in an architectural plan. |
| [INT-05](INT-05.svg) | Shared frame | Two unequal modules fit one frame. A shared unit defines the edge clearances and the space between them. |
| [INT-07](INT-07.svg) | A browser, in detail | An enlarged browser corner relates the window radius to its tab radius and content inset. Cropped edges leave the rest of the screen outside the drawing. |
| [INT-08](INT-08.svg) | The screen within the frame | Shared corner centers and an eight-pixel offset construct the frame. Symmetric vertical and horizontal margins locate the safe area within it. |
| [INT-06](INT-06.svg) | From parts to a whole | Three separate elements project into one control. Equal gaps, a common centerline, and a shared radius make the assembly rule visible. |
| [INT-10](INT-10.svg) | One corner rule | Three differently proportioned components retain a common corner radius. |
| [INT-11](INT-11.svg) | The same modules, reflowed | Three equal modules preserve their size when the available width wraps the last one onto another row. |
| [INT-12](INT-12.svg) | Position becomes value | The thumb locates sixty percent of a shared travel interval; the track clears its circular outline. |

| Code | Drawing | What it explains |

| [TIM-03](TIM-03.svg) | A week, constructed | Monday through Sunday on a measured hourly grid. One constructed circle locates a meeting on Thursday, from 10:00 to 11:00. |

| [TIM-02](TIM-02.svg) | One moment, two places | Two hour scales describe the same booking. An aligned one-hour interval stays fixed while the local time changes by three hours. |
| [TIM-08](TIM-08.svg) | Three notes, one onset | Three separately placed pitches align vertically on one shared onset to form a chord. |
| [TIM-07](TIM-07.svg) | The same interval, again | Four occurrences align to one repeated seven-day interval. |

## Empty states (EMP)

| Code | Drawing | What it explains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [EMP-03](EMP-03.svg) | An interrupted path | A measured route stops at a missing link. Its paired outlines and unresolved destination make the interruption the central gesture. |
| [EMP-05](EMP-05.svg) | The missing destination | A paired route reaches a closed end one unit before an unbuilt page. The address remains projected, but the connection is absent. |
| [EMP-06](EMP-06.svg) | A search, unanswered | A query projects into the missing position of an ordered index. The surrounding records exist; the requested one does not. |
| [EMP-08](EMP-08.svg) | A stream, caught up | Read entries occupy an evenly spaced notification stream. Its next position remains open, with no unread entry to continue it. |
| [EMP-09](EMP-09.svg) | A page, unwritten | A blank writing area repeats the page’s 1 : √2 proportion. Equal side margins locate the cursor before the first line exists. |
| [EMP-10](EMP-10.svg) | A field without observations | Calibrated axes establish a coordinate field. Its units are defined, but no observation occupies a coordinate. |
| [EMP-16](EMP-16.svg) | A week, unbooked | Seven days share a measured hour grid. Today has its place in the week; the time field contains no bookings. |
| [EMP-17](EMP-17.svg) | An image, not yet placed | Crop corners establish a 4 : 3 image area. The diagonal and unit measurements define its proportions while the image itself is absent. |
| [EMP-07](EMP-07.svg) | A cloud, out of reach | A curved connection stops before the cloud. Its separated continuation and measured gap make the missing route visible. |
| [EMP-11](EMP-11.svg) | A boundary, locked | A closed lock interrupts the access route. Its corner radius sets the inset, while a separate construction field locates the keyhole without crossing it. |
| [EMP-12](EMP-12.svg) | An envelope, unfolded | An open flap mirrors its folded position across one crease. Equal offsets and the pocket’s diagonals explain the envelope as a flat construction. |
| [EMP-13](EMP-13.svg) | A gear train, interrupted | Three gears share a common pitch. A separated drive interrupts the mechanism. |
| [EMP-14](EMP-14.svg) | A connection, apart | A mobile plug aligns with a separate socket recessed behind a thin mounting flange. The hatched support, matching contact spacing, and open gap describe the interrupted connection. |
| [EMP-15](EMP-15.svg) | A pin, unplaced | A compact pin sits just above an unresolved point in a broad coordinate field. The measured horizontal offset locates the proposed position. |
| [EMP-02](EMP-02.svg) | An empty threshold | A precise architectural threshold opens onto empty space, suggesting a destination that was never built. |
| [EMP-04](EMP-04.svg) | An unbuilt arch | An arch awaits its central keystone, turning the missing page into an unfinished architectural connection. |
| [EMP-01](EMP-01.svg) | The missing corner | A vacant module in an otherwise complete construction. Absence, described by the edges around it. |
